message.reasoning_content: We need to determine appropriate crime(s) based on facts. The person is a health administrative law enforcement officer, who failed to transfer cases of illegal medical practice to judicial authorities, instead gave administrative penalties, allowing continued illegal practice. This is abuse of power, dereliction of duty, possibly "滥用职权罪" (abuse of power) or "徇私舞弊罪" (dereliction of duty, collusion). In Chinese criminal law, there is a crime called "徇私舞弊罪" under Article 397 of Criminal Law (formerly 1997). It covers public officials who, in the performance of duties, accept bribes or collude to give false decisions, etc. Also "玩忽职守罪" (negligent duty) for failing to perform duty. However here they intentionally did not transfer, for personal economic benefit. That is "徇私舞弊罪" (collusion to pervert administration of justice). Also "滥用职权罪" (abuse of power) if they used authority to give administrative penalties instead of criminal prosecution. The examples: earlier similar case: "受贿;滥用职权" for a deputy director who accepted bribes and abused power. Here no bribe mentioned, but they used position to benefit personal and department economic tasks. So likely "滥用职权罪" (abuse of power) and maybe "徇私舞弊罪". In Chinese law, "徇私舞弊罪" is for public officials who, in the performance of duties, collude with others to give false decisions, etc. The description: "国家工作人员在执行职务时，徇私舞弊，致使国家、集体或者个人的合法权益受到重大损失的" (Article 397). This fits: they failed to transfer, causing continued illegal practice, harming public health. So answer likely: [罪名]滥用职权;徇私舞弊<eoa>. Check examples: they often list multiple separated by semicolon. So final answer: [罪名]滥用职权;徇私舞弊<eoa>.
